description:
## Why

Mega.nz offers 20GB free encrypted cloud storage, making it the only major object store with a substantial free tier. For small self-hosted NNTP deployments (personal servers, hobbyist nodes), this removes the cost barrier entirely. At 5KB average article size, 20GB holds ~4 million articles.

Mega also provides client-side E2E encryption transparently — all content stored in Mega is encrypted at rest without stoa needing to implement encryption separately.

## What

Implement MegaBlockStore for both crates/reader/src/post/ and crates/transit/src/peering/ implementing IpfsBlockStore / IpfsStore respectively.

Config:
- mega.email — Mega account email
- mega.password — Mega account password (used for key derivation; never sent to Mega servers)
- mega.folder — remote folder path to store blocks under (e.g. /stoa/blocks)

Storage layout: one file per block, named <cid>.block, inside the configured folder. Mirrors the FsBlockStore naming convention for conceptual consistency.

## Implementation options

No official Rust Mega API client exists. Two approaches:

**Option A — megatools subprocess (pragmatic first cut):** Shell out to megaput / megacat / megarm from the megatools package. Adds a system dependency (apt install megatools). All I/O via spawn_blocking + Command. Simple to implement; not suitable for high-throughput but adequate for personal deployments.

**Option B — native Mega HTTP API (proper implementation):** Implement the Mega JSON API directly over reqwest. The API is reverse-engineered but stable (used by all official Mega clients). More work upfront; no system dependency; better performance.

Start with Option A to validate the backend contract; migrate to Option B if there is demand.

## Caveats

- Mega enforces rate limits and bandwidth quotas on free accounts. This backend is not suitable for high-traffic transit nodes.
- The encryption key is derived from the Mega account password. Losing the account loses access to the blocks. Document this clearly.
- Mega is not an S3-compatible API and cannot use the existing ObjectStoreBlockBackend shared implementation.

## Acceptance

- MegaBlockStore implements IpfsBlockStore
- put_raw, put_block, get_raw, delete all work against a real Mega account in integration tests (gated behind a feature flag or environment variable to avoid requiring credentials in CI)
- Config parsing accepts [backend.mega] section
- megatools is documented as a system dependency in the README
notes: Feature-gate the integration tests behind STOA_TEST_MEGA_EMAIL / STOA_TEST_MEGA_PASSWORD env vars so CI does not require a Mega account.
